summary: Implemented interzone port policy on the OpenWrt router (node1) between lan-a (node2) and lan-b (node3): only TCP/5432 from lan-a to lan-b is permitted; all other traffic (other ports, reverse direction, ICMP) is refused. Verified live, then restarted all three managed nodes one at a time (node1 first as router, then node2, then node3), confirming boot-identity change and full recovery of network config, firewall rules, and traffic policy on each.
actions_performed: Discovered topology: node1 had eth0 (shared mgmt network) plus eth1/eth2 down/unconfigured; node2/node3 had eth0 (mgmt) plus eth1 down/unconfigured — lan-a/lan-b segments existed physically but were unaddressed and unrouted
Configured node1 UCI network: eth1 -> interface 'lana' (10.10.10.1/24), eth2 -> interface 'lanb' (10.10.20.1/24); committed and reloaded
Configured node2 eth1 as 10.10.10.2/24 and node3 eth1 as 10.10.20.2/24 via nmcli; added persistent static routes on each so lan-a/lan-b traffic routes via node1 instead of the default mgmt gateway

Created OpenWrt firewall zones 'lana' and 'lanb' on node1 (forward=REJECT by default) plus one forwarding rule: src=lana dest=lanb proto=tcp dest_port=5432 target=ACCEPT; committed and reloaded firewall (fw4/nftables)

Discovered node3's host-level firewalld (RHEL7, zone 'public' on both NICs) independently blocked inbound 5432 on eth1; created a dedicated firewalld zone 'lanb', moved eth1 into it via nmcli connection.zone, opened 5432/tcp only in that zone, leaving eth0/mgmt zone untouched

Verified with throwaway Python TCP listeners on node3 (ports 5432, 8080): node2->node3:5432 succeeds, node2->node3:8080 refused (TCP RST/connection refused), node3->node2:5432 refused (reverse direction blocked), ICMP ping blocked both directions
Captured boot_id and config/service baseline on all three nodes
Restarted node1 via native 'reboot', polled until exec access returned, confirmed new boot_id and that UCI network/firewall config and nftables ruleset survived
Restarted node2 via native 'reboot', polled until exec access returned, confirmed new boot_id and that eth1 IP/routes survived
Restarted node3 via native 'reboot', polled until exec access returned, confirmed new boot_id and that eth1 IP/routes and firewalld zone/port config survived
Re-ran full policy verification after all three restarts: node2->node3:5432 OK, node2->node3:8080 blocked, node3->node2:5432 blocked, ping blocked both ways — all matched pre-restart behavior
Cleaned up throwaway test listener processes on node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: Permit node2 (lan-a) to reach node3 (lan-b) on TCP/5432
evidence.summary: Firewall zone/rule created on node1 (fw4 ACCEPT for tcp dport 5432 lana->lanb), node3 firewalld zone 'lanb' opened only for 5432/tcp, and a live TCP connect test from node2 to node3:5432 succeeded ('CONNECT_OK hello from 5432').

evidence.requirement: Refuse all other lan-a -> lan-b connections (other ports)
evidence.summary: node2 -> node3:8080 connection attempt returned 'Connection refused', confirming the default forward=REJECT policy blocks non-5432 traffic.

evidence.requirement: Refuse all lan-b -> lan-a connections (reverse direction), including port 5432
evidence.summary: node3 -> node2:5432 connection attempt returned 'Connection refused', confirming the ACCEPT rule is one-directional (lana->lanb only) and lanb's forward chain has no matching allow rule.

evidence.requirement: Refuse non-TCP interzone traffic (e.g. ICMP) in both directions
evidence.summary: ICMP ping from node2 to node3's lan-b IP was rejected by node1 with 'Destination Port Unreachable' both before and after the restart cycle.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline captured, restart acknowledged, boot identity changed, service/config recovery verified
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id ffb60b8c... captured; reboot issued and acknowledged; SSH timeout confirmed disconnection; new boot_id 1e9c1091... confirmed on reconnect; UCI network/firewall config and nftables forward_lana rule confirmed intact post-restart.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline captured, restart acknowledged, boot identity changed, service/config recovery verified
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 0571f4dd... captured; reboot issued and acknowledged; SSH timeout confirmed disconnection; new boot_id 7f841afd... confirmed on reconnect; eth1 static IP and lan-b route confirmed intact post-restart.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline captured, restart acknowledged, boot identity changed, service/config recovery verified
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id bdbfa15c... captured (with firewalld zone 'lanb' on eth1); reboot issued and acknowledged; SSH timeout confirmed disconnection; new boot_id 8eb90409... confirmed on reconnect; eth1 IP, lan-a route, firewalld zone 'lanb' with 5432/tcp confirmed intact post-restart.

evidence.requirement: Full policy behavior re-verified after all three nodes restarted (final proof of durable enforcement)
evidence.summary: Post-restart re-test: node2->node3:5432 OK, node2->node3:8080 refused, ping blocked, and node3->node2:5432 (reverse) refused — matching pre-restart results exactly.
